notes:
I matched 62 of the 65 stations to a row, 61 with high confidence. Two stations get null: Fair Isle (an observer's station; Findlay 1887 has no light there) and Hynish Signal Tower (Skerryvore's shore station, not a light). North Carr L.V. is the one doubtful match (medium).

Things to check:
1) North Carr L.V. → row 263. Findlay 1887 only says 'Lightvessel proposed with fixed bright light', yet the reports list the Carr Rock lightship from 1885. Your rule says null for a light-vessel not yet placed. I gave the row because it is a real entry with a position, but its character is only the proposed one. Choose between using it and null, and check when the vessel was actually placed.
2) Ailsa Craig: Findlay gives established 1886, but the reports list it from 1885 (map 109B@1885). Check whether the 1885 report really includes it or whether the year was assigned wrongly.
3) Hoy Low and Hoy High both get row 303, a single entry with two items. Item 1 is the high light (fixed bright or red, 108 ft tower) and item 2 is the low light (fixed bright). When you take each light's character, take the right item.
4) Some single rows hold several lights. Arnish Point → 318 (Stornoway): use item 1 only. Isle of May → 264 (main and low light), Pentland Skerries → 299, Girdle Ness → 276 and Pladda → 343 (two lights each). No Scottish station has its lights split over separate rows, so extra_rows is empty everywhere.
5) Easy-to-confuse names. Fladda is row 330 ('Phladda Island'); Pladda is row 343. Sanda (Kintyre) is row 339; Start Point (Orkney, on Sanday) is row 306. Montrose Ness (row 273) is Scurdie Ness, not Montrose Harbour (row 274). Loch Ryan is row 356, not Stranraer (row 357).
6) Names that differ from the reports: Findlay prints Corran as 'Loch Eil', Holy Isle as 'Lamlash Harbour', Skervuile as 'Sgeir Maoile or Iron Rock', Rhuvaal as 'RUDHA MHAIL', Eilean Glas as 'GLASS ISLAND', Out Skerries as 'WHALSEY SKERRIES' and Muckle Flugga as 'NORTH UNST'. In each case the descriptions and positions confirm the match.
7) Findlay lists the Orkney and Shetland lights in the opposite direction to the reports (Auskerry → Start Point → North Ronaldsha → Sumburgh → Bressay → Whalsey → North Unst). Several west-coast runs are also in a different order. I matched these by position and description, not by order.
